en: The Method for Reciting the Single Seal of the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
extracted from the *Sāhasrabhuja-sāhasranetra-vidhi* by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā of Daxingshan Monastery.
Translated by Amoghavajra by Imperial Decree: Now, when a practitioner wishes to perform recitation, they should first recite the Mantra of Purity seven times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ ṭiṭṭibha svāhā. By reciting this mantra...
Then one attains purity of the three karmas;
one becomes bathed in the water of the Dharma of merit, purifying both body and mind;
then one binds the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Interlace the two hands to form fists;
extend the fingers of the *dhyāna-mudrā* outward and hold them straight up, and it is thus completed.
Recite the heart mantra seven times.
The mantra is:
Oṃ āḥ lu li ka svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
This constitutes the samaya.
Furthermore, bind the previous mudrā and recite the mantra three times;
then, with the mudrā, circumambulate to the left three times.
This accomplishes the expulsion of all demonic obstacles.
Furthermore, by forming the previous mudrā and reciting the mantra three times,
and then rotating the mudrā clockwise three times, one establishes the boundary (sīmābandha).
Then, visualize an eight-petaled lotus flower in front of one's body.
Again, form the previous mudrā and recite the mantra seven times,
beckoning it toward oneself with the hand of meditative concentration (dhyāna-pāramitā).
Then the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
together with all the holy assemblies of the Lotus Family,
all came to assemble.
Then, with both hands holding the vessel of *argha* perfumed water,
offer it to the forehead while reciting the mantra seven times,
visualizing that the assembly of holy ones is being bathed.
Furthermore, by forming the aforementioned mudrā and reciting the mantra seven times,
one accomplishes the offering of a lotus seat.
Again, by forming the aforementioned mudrā and reciting the mantra three times, [the same is accomplished].
This constitutes the offering of fragrant ointment.
Furthermore, by binding the aforementioned mudrā and reciting the mantra three times,
it becomes the offering of flower garlands.
Furthermore, by forming the aforementioned mudrā and reciting the mantra three times,
one accomplishes various kinds of sublime celestial food and drink for offering.
Again, by forming the aforementioned mudrā and reciting the mantra three times...
This constitutes the offering of lamps and candles.
Furthermore, forming the aforementioned mudrā at the heart,
one should recite the mantra seven times while visualizing oneself seated within the center of an eight-petaled lotus pedestal.
Endowed with the full perfection of the marks and signs and majestic radiance, he is equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Upon each of the eight petals of the lotus flower:
In each [lotus] there is a Tathāgata entered into meditative absorption,
facing toward Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The practitioner should contemplate them in this manner until they are extremely clear.
Raising the mudrā above the crown of the head, disperse it;
then take the rosary, coil it within the palms, place the hands together at the heart,
and recite the mantra for empowering the rosary seven times.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vīra-sajñā-maṇi-lasvāhā. Then, place both hands at the heart.
Form the five fingers into the shape of an unopened lotus flower at the heart;
recite the mantra there,
neither too slowly nor too quickly, clearly and distinctly, without making any sound.
While reciting in a state of tranquility, move one bead for each syllable of the mantra as it is uttered.
Within the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra), omit the first and last syllables.
During the recitation, do not allow the mind to become distracted.
With body and mind stilled and tranquil, without further shifting one's focus,
one should contemplate only the *iṣṭadevatā* while reciting with single-minded concentration.
Then, one should visualize an eight-petaled lotus flower above one's own body.
One visualizes the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, complete with all the marks and signs of perfection, situated within a lunar disc;
furthermore, one contemplates one's own body as being identical to that of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, without any distinction.
When the recitation count is complete,
hold the rosary above your head, arouse a mind of compassion, and make this great vow:
"Whatever all sentient beings may desire..."
If one wishes for the supreme aspirations of the world to be swiftly fulfilled,
then restore the *ānkuśa* jewel to its original place.
Furthermore, forming the aforementioned mudrā at the heart, recite the mantra seven times.
This constitutes the samaya.
Furthermore, empower one's own body at five locations with the mudrā;
these so-called five locations are the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat.
Recite each mantra once.
Perform the empowerment by scattering [flowers] from the mudrā at the crown of the head.
Again, bind the previous mudrā and present the five kinds of offerings as before.
Reciting the mantra once for each constitutes a vast offering.
Then, holding argha water with both hands,
offer it to the forehead while reciting the mantra once.
Furthermore, by binding the previous mudrā and rotating it once to the left, the boundary is dissolved.
Again, bind the previous mudrā and cast the *dhyāna-aṅguli* (thumb) outward while reciting the mantra three times.
Raising the mudrā and placing it upon the crown of the head accomplishes the ritual of escorting all the noble assemblies.
Furthermore, bind the aforementioned mudrā and consecrate the five places of one's own body.
Recite the mantra once for each;
this constitutes the donning of the armor.
Then, perform the scattering mudrā above the crown of the head.
If a practitioner thus relies upon these essential points of the secret dharma,
reciting with sincerity and applying the mind to practice,
all that they undertake will swiftly attain accomplishment.
May all mundane and supramundane aspirations be fulfilled;
may karmic obstacles be eliminated and samādhi manifest before you;
and without changing this very body, may you soar through space with sovereign ease according to your will.
One shall immediately travel to the pure lands of the ten directions to serve the various Buddhas and swiftly attain unsurpassed bodhi.
Regarding the method for reciting the heart-mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva with one mudrā, the *Eight Houses Secret Record* states:
The Method for Reciting the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva with One Seal. By Jin Amogha (Jin means "Benevolent";
Amogha is the name of the Great Master Ci-jiao).
This original manuscript was brought back by Jikaku Daishi.
